key_insight: Multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence can non-destructively separate interface and bulk degradation in perovskite solar cells, revealing that PEABF4 initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but later accelerates depth-spreading recombination losses under heat.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic for designing and validating interface treatments while tracking how thermal stress shifts recombination from surface-limited to absorber-wide degradation.
method: Use wavelength-dependent PL to probe different excitation depths without destroying the device.
Compare PL decay signatures before and during thermal aging to distinguish interface-dominated vs bulk-dominated losses.
Support interpretation with diffusion-recombination simulations linking PL changes to surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PEABF4-treated stacks show reduced interfacial recombination initially, but after thermal aging the PL decay broadens deeper into the absorber, consistent with worsening depth-dependent degradation.
watch_item: PL-based depth interpretation depends on the accuracy of the optical/diffusion model, so calibration against independent structural or electrical measurements is important.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
